episodes.label: The Ovulation Signal and the Outcome — Enclomiphene vs. Zuclomiphene Isomer Kinetics, Estrogen Receptor Antagonist Conformation (PDB 6VPF), Timed Mid-Luteal Progesterone vs. PPCOS II Live-Birth Endpoints
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 118: Enclomiphene vs. Zuclomiphene Isomer Kinetics, Estrogen Receptor Antagonist Conformation (PDB 6VPF), Timed Mid-Luteal Progesterone vs. PPCOS II Live-Birth Endpoints. A follicle grows, the next scan shows it has collapsed, and progesterone rises. The Critical Care Clinician follows what each measurement establishes for a woman seeking pregnancy. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows clomiphene from a Merrell patent to an estrogen-receptor crystal and two distinct concentration curves. The patient, dates and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook’s *Volume II: Sports Pharmacology, Ergogenics and Metabolic Modulators*, dossier 2.1, supplies the starting reference to clomiphene as a hormonal-axis drug. The fertility episode draws on separate evidence in women. Historical sources use polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). The international guideline adopted polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in its May 2026 terminology update. Pharmacology notebook · International guideline terminology update

episodes.label: The Two Hands of Ritalin — d-threo vs. l-threo Methylphenidate Stereochemistry at Human DAT (PDB 8Y2G), Enantioselective CES1 Presystemic Hydrolysis to Ritalinic Acid & Achiral vs. Chiral LC–MS/MS Matrices

Notebook anchor. Chapter Four, “Psychostimulants: Basic and Clinical Pharmacology,” by McCreary, Müller and Filip in *International Review of Neurobiology* (2015) introduces methylphenidate among drugs that alter monoamine uptake. Start at an ADHD follow-up and trace the patient’s changing ability to work, circulating parent drug and a urinary metabolite. Pharmacology notebook · Chapter record

episodes.label: The Weight Loss and the Warning — Rimonabant (SR141716A) CB1 Inverse Agonism (PDB 5TGZ), RIO Metabolic Biomarker Gains vs. CRESCENDO Psychiatric Adverse Events & European Withdrawal
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 110: Rimonabant (SR141716A) CB1 Inverse Agonism (PDB 5TGZ), RIO Metabolic Biomarker Gains vs. CRESCENDO Psychiatric Adverse Events & European Withdrawal. In a European clinic in 2008, a man’s weight and blood tests move in the hoped-for direction. The visit changes when he describes how little pleasure he gets from the things he used to enjoy. The Critical Care Clinician follows the measurements and the interview. The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs how an antagonist of cannabinoid effects became an inverse agonist in receptor experiments and why a later trial had to count clinical events directly. The patient, dialogue and individual measurements are fictional. Chapter One, “The Endocannabinoid Signaling System in the CNS: A Primer” (2015), in the live Pharmacology notebook introduces SR141716A and inverse agonism. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The First Dose That Slowed the Heart — Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 107: Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials. At the sixth hour of a first fingolimod observation, an atrial impulse reaches the ECG and fails to reach the ventricles. Two weeks later, the lab reports a sharp fall in circulating lymphocytes. The Critical Care Clinician follows conduction, perfusion and the blood count. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows an active phosphate ester into a receptor and then follows the receptor off the lymphocyte surface. The patient, dialogue and individual values are fictional. David S. Miller’s “ABC Transporter Regulation by Signaling at the Blood–Brain Barrier” (2014) in the live Pharmacology notebook provides the rat brain-capillary starting point. Drug development, human trials and bedside interpretation draw on separate sources. Pharmacology notebook · Primary capillary experiment

episodes.label: The Signal Behind the Session — Hofmann's Psilocybin Isolation to Psilocin–5-HT2A Cryo-EM (PDB 9AS7), Ketanserin Blocking & Cimbi-36 PET Occupancy, Supervised Hemodynamics & Goodwin/EPISODE Depression Trial Masking
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 104: Hofmann's Psilocybin Isolation to Psilocin–5-HT2A Cryo-EM (PDB 9AS7), Ketanserin Blocking & Cimbi-36 PET Occupancy, Supervised Hemodynamics & Goodwin/EPISODE Depression Trial Masking. A blood pressure cuff inflates midway through a supervised psilocybin research visit. Weeks later, an interviewer asks the participant how she has been sleeping and whether ordinary things interest her again. The Critical Care Clinician follows those two clocks. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows a phosphate ester from a Sandoz chemistry paper to a modeled contact in human 5-HT₂A. The participant, dialogue, observations and individual numbers are fictional. The live Pharmacology notebook’s Chapter 17, “Hallucinogens,” from The Effects of Drug Abuse on the Human Nervous System (2014), introduces psilocybin, psilocin and the antagonist experiments. The primary studies below supply the quantitative evidence. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Signal That Tightened the Airway — SRS-A to Cysteinyl Leukotrienes, Zafirlukast Bound to Human CysLT1R (PDB 6RZ5), Inhaled LTD4 Bronchoprovocation vs. Chronic Asthma Trials & Idiosyncratic Hepatotoxicity
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 101: SRS-A to Cysteinyl Leukotrienes, Zafirlukast Bound to Human CysLT1R (PDB 6RZ5), Inhaled LTD4 Bronchoprovocation vs. Chronic Asthma Trials & Idiosyncratic Hepatotoxicity. A woman with asthma exhales 400 mL more in the first second after an inhaled bronchodilator. Weeks later, a different measurement changes the course of her care. The Critical Care Clinician follows airflow, symptoms and liver chemistry. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows a lipid signal from its synthesis to the airway receptor and the drug that occupies its pocket. The case, values and dialogue are fictional. Chapter 9, “The Eicosanoids: Cyclooxygenase, Lipoxygenase, and Epoxygenase Pathways” (2016), in the Pharmacology notebook introduces LTC₄, LTD₄ and LTE₄, their receptors and their effects on the airway. Primary studies establish the drug-specific evidence. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Channel That Opened Longer — CFTR G551D Open-Probability Defect, Ivacaftor (VX-770) Transmembrane Lasso/TM8 Hinge Binding (PDB 6O2P), STRIVE Sweat-Chloride vs. FEV1 Readouts & CFF Biomarker Interpretation
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 96: CFTR G551D Open-Probability Defect, Ivacaftor (VX-770) Transmembrane Lasso/TM8 Hinge Binding (PDB 6O2P), STRIVE Sweat-Chloride vs. FEV1 Readouts & CFF Biomarker Interpretation. Sweat chloride concentration falls to about half its pretreatment value. A spirometer shows a smaller change in a different unit. The patient, clinical values and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is H. Criss Hartzell’s 2010 Chapter 1, “Chloride Channels: An Historical Perspective,” especially section C on cystic fibrosis and CFTR agonists. The chapter predates U.S. ivacaftor approval. Pharmacology notebook · Hartzell, Chapter 1

episodes.label: The Blood Pressure Drug That Reached the Classroom — Guanfacine from Centrally Acting Antihypertensive to Prefrontal Alpha-2A HCN Regulation, Cryo-EM (PDB 7EJ8) & Pediatric ADHD/Tic RCTs
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 87: Guanfacine from Centrally Acting Antihypertensive to Prefrontal Alpha-2A HCN Regulation, Cryo-EM (PDB 7EJ8) & Pediatric ADHD/Tic RCTs. An 11-year-old wants to finish the first problem on a worksheet before losing their place. Their parent asks whether the same medicine might help the shoulder jerks and throat sounds that interrupt reading aloud. The Critical Care Clinician follows symptoms, daily function and circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist traces an antihypertensive patent through receptor assays, primate recordings and trials with different clinical endpoints. The patient, observations and host dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Andreas Hartmann’s 2013 chapter Clinical Pharmacology of Nondopaminergic Drugs in Tourette Syndrome, section 2.2 on guanfacine. Pharmacology notebook · Hartmann chapter

episodes.label: The Patch That Changed a Pain Fiber — Caterina's 1997 TRPV1 Cloning, Vanilloid Pocket Cryo-EM (PDB 7LPE), Reversible Epidermal Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization (Kennedy) & 8% Capsaicin Patch Trials
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 85: Caterina's 1997 TRPV1 Cloning, Vanilloid Pocket Cryo-EM (PDB 7LPE), Reversible Epidermal Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization (Kennedy) & 8% Capsaicin Patch Trials. A sock hurts a woman’s feet. A concentrated patch activates the channel that makes chili feel hot, yet her pain diary later records less burning. The patient, measurements and dialogue are fictional. The notebook anchor is Roman V. Frolov and Matti Weckström’s chapter “Harnessing the Flow of Excitation: TRP, Voltage-Gated Na⁺, and Voltage-Gated Ca²⁺ Channels in Contemporary Medicine,” published online December 10, 2015 and in the 2016 volume. episodes.label: The Signal That Stopped the Migraine — Humphrey's 5-HT1B/1D Vascular Hypothesis, Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (US4816470 / US5037845), 5-HT1B Cryo-EM Comparator (PDB 6G79) & Human PET/MRA
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 83: Humphrey's 5-HT1B/1D Vascular Hypothesis, Subcutaneous Sumatriptan (US4816470 / US5037845), 5-HT1B Cryo-EM Comparator (PDB 6G79) & Human PET/MRA. A woman recognizes her usual migraine, but vomiting has made it difficult to keep fluids and tablets down. The Critical Care Clinician checks the time course, neurologic examination and vascular history. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows Glaxo’s GR43175 from vascular experiments and patent claims to human receptor pharmacology. The patient, observations and dialogue are fictional. The notebook source is Bockaert and colleagues’ 2010 chapter on serotonin receptor classification and signaling, specifically its discussion of 5-HT₁B, 5-HT₁D, 5-HT₁E and 5-HT₁F. Pharmacology notebook · Bockaert et al., receptor chapter

episodes.label: The Burn That Came Before Relief — TRPV1 Cloning (Caterina 1997), Reversible Epidermal PGP 9.5 Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization & 8% Capsaicin Patch Neuropathic Pain Trials
episodes.notes: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

episodes.label: The Odor They Learned to Detect — Unilateral Nostril Androstenone Induction (Mainland 2002), Human OR7D4 Genetic Polymorphisms (Keller 2007) & Olfactory Training
episodes.notes: Peripheral vs. central plasticity in human olfaction: Mainland et al.'s (2002) single-nostril exposure experiment showing contralateral transfer of acquired androstenone sensitivity, Keller et al.'s (2007) and Lunde et al.'s (2012) OR7D4 RT/WM receptor variants governing odor intensity and valence in pork taint, and Gillmeister et al.'s (2025) olfactory perceptual training.

episodes.label: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

episodes.label: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

episodes.label: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits

(1976) 12-fold total serum rise with undetectable free digoxin, Jortani et al. (1999) ultrafiltrate immunoassay bias across platforms, Ujhelyi et al. (1993) delayed free-digoxin rebound in renal dysfunction, and Gerritsma et al. (2025) chronic digoxin cardiogenic shock.

episodes.notes: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

episodes.label: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. episodes.label: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

episodes.label: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

episodes.label: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
episodes.notes: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

(2008) 1H-MRS genetics, Ser47–Asp166 patatin dyad, ubiquitylation-resistant I148M accumulation on lipid droplets sequestering CGI-58/ABHD5 away from ATGL (Wang et al. 2019), and phase I/IIb GalNAc-ASO AZD2693 MRI-PDFF reductions vs. FORTUNA histologic fibrosis endpoints.

episodes.notes: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

episodes.label: Warfarin & the Three Clocks of Bleeding — Spoiled Sweet Clover, VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139, Chiral S/R-Warfarin m/z 307→161, 4F-PCC vs. INR & Serial ICH CT
episodes.notes: From spoiled sweet-clover hemorrhagic disease and Link's 1947 patent to human VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139 crystal contacts, chiral LC-MS/MS separation of S- and R-warfarin (sharing m/z 307->161), and separating the three clinical clocks of drug clearance, factor replacement (4F-PCC vs. plasma), and intracerebral hematoma expansion.

episodes.label: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
episodes.notes: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).
